root_cause.text: The recovery_cnt fence in __iommu_group_set_domain_internal() incorrectly blocked IOMMU_SET_DOMAIN_MUST_SUCCEED callers during device reset, preventing group->domain from being updated before the domain is freed, leading to a use-after-free when pci_dev_reset_iommu_done() later re-attaches the stale domain pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that the rejection of IOMMU_SET_DOMAIN_MUST_SUCCEED callers during recovery triggers a WARN_ON and can cause a UAF because "the domain would be freed anyway in these nofail paths while group->domain is still pointing to it." The patch fixes this by allowing the must-succeed callers through the recovery_cnt fence and adding a per-device blocked check instead.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix domain attach during device recovery by allowing the operation to succeed when the IOMMU_SET_DOMAIN_MUST_SUCCEED flag is set, instead of unconditionally returning -EBUSY.
intent_record.what: Added a condition to the existing check `if (group->recovery_cnt)` to also require that the `IOMMU_SET_DOMAIN_MUST_SUCCEED` flag is not set before returning -EBUSY. Updated the comment to reflect this.
intent_record.how: Previously, any concurrent attach during device recovery (when `recovery_cnt > 0`) was always rejected with -EBUSY. Now, if the caller passes `IOMMU_SET_DOMAIN_MUST_SUCCEED` flag, the rejection is bypassed, allowing the domain set to proceed even during recovery.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip setting domain for devices under recovery (marked blocked) to avoid interfering with the recovery process.
intent_record.what: Inside __iommu_group_set_domain_internal, added a check to skip devices for which gdev->blocked is true, preventing domain change for those devices.
intent_record.how: At runtime, during domain switching, devices that are under recovery (blocked) will be skipped, so their domain remains unchanged until recovery completes.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit adds a check in __iommu_group_set_domain_internal() at line 2437-2442 that unconditionally returns -EBUSY when group->resetting_domain is set. This blocks all concurrent domain changes during device reset, including IOMMU_SET_DOMAIN_MUST_SUCCEED callers that need to update group->domain before the old domain is freed. As a result, pci_dev_reset_iommu_done() later re-attaches the stale group->domain pointer, leading to a use-after-free. No exception for MUST_SUCCEED is provided, so the vulnerable construct is present and unfixed.
